insight_title: Anti-obesity GLP-1 criteria embed concurrency blocks and 6-month renewal gates
drug_or_class: Anti-obesity agents, including Wegovy, Saxenda, and Zepbound
why_it_matters: Manufacturers may focus on initial BMI criteria and miss the utilization-management details that can limit persistence: no concurrent weight-loss drug, no concurrent DPP-4 inhibitor with anti-obesity GLP-1s, documented height/weight/BMI, and proof of maintained weight loss for renewal.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Initial criteria require attestation against concurrent weight-loss drugs and against using Wegovy, Saxenda, or Zepbound with a DPP-4 inhibitor. Adult renewal requires documentation of maintained weight loss of at least 5% from baseline; initial and renewal approvals are each 6 months.
validation_note: Confirmed in the June 3, 2025 Michigan P&T materials under Anti-Obesity Agents PA criteria revision; renewal language continues on page 10.

insight_title: Michigan will narrow anti-obesity GLP-1 authorization to morbid obesity on January 1, 2026
why_it_matters: This creates a concrete pull-through and reauthorization risk date for existing and prospective Wegovy/Zepbound/Saxenda access, while preserving approved prior authorizations only through the rest of their 6-month term.
evidence_quote_or_summary: MDHHS reported it would revise coverage policies to limit anti-obesity GLP-1 receptor agonists exclusively to individuals classified as morbidly obese, effective 1/1/2026; existing PAs approved before 1/1/2026 would be honored for the remainder of the 6-month authorization.
validation_note: Confirmed in December 2, 2025 draft minutes embedded in the March 3, 2026 Michigan P&T packet.

insight_title: Outcomes-based contracting preferences are explicit and contactable
therapeutic_area: High-cost drugs / gene and specialty therapies
drug_or_class: Zolgensma, Mavyret, Zynteglo, Lyfgenia, Casgevy, Elevidys and other high-cost drugs
why_it_matters: Michigan discloses the kinds of outcomes arrangements it prefers, making this a rare public roadmap for value-based contracting approaches and manufacturer outreach.
evidence_quote_or_summary: MDHHS says it has CMS approval to pursue outcomes/value-based purchasing for high-cost drugs, lists six active agreements, prefers MDHHS staff tracking outcomes instead of third-party aggregators, and prefers outcomes trackable through claims data, such as small orphan populations or volume/adherence outcomes.
validation_note: Confirmed in Michigan P&T materials; the later December 2025 minutes repeat the six active agreements and same preferences.

insight_title: Alyftrek access is routed through MPPL PA and an MHP pharmacy carveout
why_it_matters: The criteria require operational documentation beyond diagnosis: genetic testing results must be faxed, baseline FEV1 and BMI must be documented, liver tests must be assessed and monitored, and prescribing must involve an experienced pulmonologist.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Alyftrek is marked 'Not a PDL class - Add to MPPL with PA' and noted as falling in an existing MHP pharmacy carveout class. Criteria include age at least 6, CF diagnosis, responsive CFTR mutation confirmed by genetic testing with test results faxed, baseline FEV1/BMI documentation, LFT monitoring, pulmonologist involvement, and 1-year approval.
validation_note: Confirmed in the June 3, 2025 agenda new-drug review and public-comment list.

insight_title: Final PDL authority sits with DOM leadership, while net cost and rebate pool leverage are explicit inputs
why_it_matters: Committee votes are not the final coverage action. Manufacturers need to track the Medicaid Executive Director approval step, the 30-day notice/go-live cycle, and Mississippi's reliance on supplemental rebates through the Sovereign States Drug Consortium.
evidence_quote_or_summary: DOM states that committee recommendation and net cost are both considered; DOM aggressively pursues supplemental rebates through the SSDC pool. Committee votes and MedImpact preferred/non-preferred recommendations go to the Medicaid Executive Director for final approval, with public notice 30 days before the new PDL goes live.
validation_note: Confirmed in May 13, 2025 Mississippi P&T minutes; the February 10, 2026 draft minutes restate the same governance pattern.

insight_title: Industry gets a predictable but tightly rationed comment window
why_it_matters: Mississippi gives pharma a reliable engagement mechanism but limits execution: online registration opens 30 days before each meeting, committee members receive reviews 2-3 weeks prior, and industry designees get 3 minutes per drug.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The minutes say online registration opens 30 days before each meeting; committee members receive Therapeutic Class Reviews electronically about 2-3 weeks before the meeting; advocacy groups and pharmaceutical industry designees have 3 minutes per group or per drug, with MedImpact calling registered speakers and enforcing the time limit.
validation_note: Confirmed in the May 2025 minutes and repeated in February 2026 draft minutes with the same 3-minute rule.

insight_title: July 2026 provider notice would prefer both oral and injectable antiobesity entrants
why_it_matters: The May 2026 notice shows a future antiobesity access change before the effective date, including an oral GLP-1 pathway signal and a preferred status move for Zepbound, pending committee and DOM approvals.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The Provider Notice says PDL changes are effective July 1, 2026, pending approval by the P&T Committee, DOM, and DOM's Executive Director. Under new preferred drugs, Antiobesity Select Agents include Foundayo and Zepbound.
validation_note: Confirmed in Mississippi July 1, 2026 Provider Notice; status is pending final approvals per the notice.

insight_title: Humira loses preferred status while multiple adalimumab and ustekinumab biosimilars gain preferred positioning
drug_or_class: Cytokine and CAM antagonists, Humira, adalimumab biosimilars, ustekinumab biosimilars
why_it_matters: This is a payer-significant biosimilar displacement signal: the recommendation included preferred moves for several biosimilars, non-preferred moves for Humira, and grandfathering language.
evidence_quote_or_summary: In October 2025 minutes, MedImpact recommended moving Yuflyma, Cyltezo, Hadlima, adalimumab-aaty autoinject, Imuldosa, Selarsdi, and Pyzchiva to preferred, adding Anzupgo to non-preferred, and the committee adopted the recommendation with grandfathering.
validation_note: Confirmed in the October 21, 2025 draft P&T minutes; separate Minnesota minutes show a similar Humira-to-nonpreferred pattern.

insight_title: SmartPA can approve non-preferred drugs without a call when claims data show preferred-agent trials
why_it_matters: The access barrier is not just formulary status; it is whether the paid-claims history contains the diagnoses, procedures, or prior preferred-agent trials needed for automated approval.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Missouri says non-preferred agents may be transparently approved through SmartPA after a trial of preferred agents paid for by MO HealthNet. Claims are screened against other drug claims, diagnoses, and procedures; approvals occur without a call over 75% of the time, while non-matches reject and require call-center override.
validation_note: Confirmed in Missouri PDL FAQs; HTML source has no page number.

insight_title: DPAC public comment is three minutes per medication, with manufacturers capped in aggregate
why_it_matters: Missouri's DPAC page exposes both the timing and tactical limit for manufacturer testimony; the same page publishes quarterly class-edit proposal links that can identify upcoming review categories before decisions are finalized.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The meeting-materials page says any interested party may provide clinically relevant public comment for up to 3 minutes per medication under review, registration must be completed before the meeting, and manufacturers receive 3 minutes in the aggregate per medication.
validation_note: Confirmed in Missouri DPAC meeting materials page; HTML source has no page number.

insight_title: Manufacturer submissions must be short, early, clinical, and non-pricing
why_it_matters: Montana is unusually explicit about what manufacturer evidence the Board wants: new peer-reviewed randomized comparative or controlled trials with true health outcomes, not pricing, submitted at least 7 days before the meeting.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The agenda instructs submitters to email written comments/clinical information to PDL@mt.gov at least 7 days prior, limit clinical information to 2 pages and new information since last review, says randomized comparative or controlled trials with true health outcomes are most helpful, and says not to provide pricing information.
validation_note: Confirmed in Montana April 2024 DUR meeting agenda; similar language appears in other Montana agendas.

insight_title: Wegovy MASH coverage requires objective fibrosis evidence and long-cycle renewal proof
why_it_matters: Montana's criteria create a high-evidence renewal burden for MASH use: adults need noncirrhotic MASH with F2-F3 fibrosis documented by FibroScan-like ultrasound or biopsy, and renewal requires improvement/no worsening at 12 months and at least every 4 years thereafter.
evidence_quote_or_summary: For MASH, members must be adults with noncirrhotic MASH and F2-F3 fibrosis diagnosed by specialized ultrasound or liver biopsy, have diet/exercise/lifestyle modification, use a gastroenterology/hepatology specialist or consult, and at renewal provide improvement/no worsening documentation by specialized ultrasound or biopsy.
validation_note: Confirmed in Montana November 2025 DUR/Formulary meeting material.

insight_title: Repatha MACE expansion still requires two high-intensity statins plus ezetimibe
why_it_matters: A broadened MACE indication does not remove step therapy. Montana requires prior high-intensity statin and ezetimibe experience and prohibits concomitant PCSK9 use; renewal requires positive LDL-C response documentation.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The Repatha update adds reduced MACE risk for adults at increased risk, including diabetes mellitus as an evidentiary pathway, but requires trial and inadequate response or contraindication to at least two high-intensity statins at maximum tolerated dose in combination with ezetimibe. Renewal requires documentation of positive clinical response such as LDL-C reduction.
validation_note: Confirmed in Montana November 2025 Repatha criteria update.

insight_title: Montana PDL blocks bypassing criteria with samples, patient assistance, or cash pay
why_it_matters: This limits common bridge and hub tactics: Montana says those histories do not support grandfathering if they were used to bypass criteria or PDL placement.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The May 2026 PDL states that grandfathering of medications does not apply if samples, patient assistance, or cash pay have been used to bypass criteria or PDL placement.
validation_note: Confirmed on page 1 of Montana Healthcare Programs PDL revised May 1, 2026.

insight_title: Nebraska's PDL economics are reviewed alongside explicit rebate and savings reports
why_it_matters: Nebraska discloses a structured clinical-then-economic process: rebates matter especially when drugs are therapeutically equivalent, and PBM reporting includes quarterly rebate status, PDL compliance, and savings.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Nebraska guidelines say preferred drugs are based on clinical effectiveness, safety, and outcomes; when drugs are therapeutically equivalent or nearly equivalent, cost including rebates is considered. Economic analysis uses Nebraska utilization, CMS rebates, and supplemental rebates; PBM provides quarterly rebate-agreement status, PDL compliance, and savings reports.
validation_note: Confirmed in Nebraska PDL Guidelines.

insight_title: Nebraska's opioid controls combine a lower MME ceiling with strict MOUD guardrails
why_it_matters: The barrier is both dose and indication. The PDL lowered the opioid dose ceiling to 120 MME/day, and buprenorphine products for OUD are not approved for pain management and require prescriber and concomitant-opioid checks.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The PDL highlights that maximum opioid dose covered decreased from 150 to 120 MME/day beginning September 1, 2020. For opioid dependence treatments, non-preferred buprenorphine products require OUD diagnosis, are not approved for pain management, require verification of the prescriber's X DEA license number, no concomitant opioids, and preferred-drug failure or patient-specific documentation.
validation_note: Confirmed in Nebraska PDL September 1, 2020; included because the criteria are explicit and operationally detailed.

insight_title: CGRP migraine prevention requires both migraine burden and two conventional therapy trials
why_it_matters: The CGRP barrier is not just preferred status: Nebraska requires quantified migraine burden and prior treatment history; Aimovig has an additional step through Emgality or Ajovy unless there is patient-specific justification.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Aimovig, Ajovy, and Emgality 120 mg require more than 4 migraines per month for more than 3 months and failure of more than a 1-month trial of two therapies from AAN/AHS guideline categories. Aimovig additionally requires a trial of Emgality 120 mg or Ajovy or a clinical patient-specific reason a preferred agent cannot be used.
validation_note: Confirmed in Nebraska PDL September 1, 2020 migraine criteria.

insight_title: Wegovy PA was revised for MASH, but dosage-form indication differentiation was required
why_it_matters: The Board did not simply approve a new indication; it required the PA form to distinguish dosage forms by indication, which can affect pharmacy benefit implementation and denial logic.
evidence_quote_or_summary: January 2026 draft minutes say new indication criteria for MASH were added to the existing Wegovy PA form, and the Board approved the form with revisions to differentiate the correct dosage forms with their indications. Novo Nordisk representatives commented on the Wegovy PA form.
validation_note: Confirmed in Nebraska January 13, 2026 draft DUR Board minutes.

insight_title: Nevada's public-comment route is agenda-bound and best used before the meeting
why_it_matters: Nevada gives manufacturers and advocates a route into meeting materials, but the agenda warns that no action can be taken unless the matter is already listed as an action item.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The October 2025 agenda encourages advance written comments so they can be included in meeting materials, says comments may be submitted to rxinfo@nvha.nv.gov, limits comment to 3 minutes per person, and says no action may be taken on public comment unless the matter is specifically included on the agenda as an action item.
validation_note: Confirmed in Nevada October 16, 2025 DUR agenda.

insight_title: Rezdiffra step edit was modified to allow specialist justification when Wegovy is expected ineffective
why_it_matters: This is a precise Board-level amendment to a proposed criteria package. It creates a pathway around a Wegovy step requirement for Rezdiffra when specialist justification supports it.
evidence_quote_or_summary: In October 2025 minutes, Prime presented MASH criteria for Wegovy and Rezdiffra. The Board approved Rezdiffra criteria with added statement to the step-edit requirement allowing a specialist-justification option if there is reason to expect Wegovy to be ineffective for the recipient's specific treatment; Wegovy criteria were approved separately.
validation_note: Confirmed in Nevada October 16, 2025 DUR minutes; MCO medical directors approved proposed criteria as presented before Board amendment.

insight_title: Zepbound criteria and quantity limits passed without public comment
why_it_matters: Nevada's April 2025 minutes show Zepbound moved through criteria and QL adoption with no public comment and no Board discussion, after all listed MCO representatives approved the proposed criteria.
evidence_quote_or_summary: For Zepbound, telephonic/web comments were opened but none were provided; Prime reviewed proposed criteria and utilization; Health Plan of Nevada, SilverSummit, Molina, and Anthem approved the criteria as presented; the Board moved to approve the criteria as presented by Prime Therapeutics.
validation_note: Confirmed in Nevada April 17, 2025 DUR minutes.

insight_title: Public hearing testimony requires 48-hour notice and written materials are capped at five pages
why_it_matters: New Hampshire's public hearing gives a clear but narrow engagement window before DUR review: speakers must preregister 48 hours ahead, speaking is limited to 3-5 minutes, and written materials must arrive 48 hours ahead and stay under 5 pages.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The September 2025 agenda says the public hearing solicits views on NH Medicaid FFS pharmacy PA criteria; commenters must notify DHHS at least 48 hours in advance, speaking is limited to 3-5 minutes depending on preregistered speakers, and written material must be received at least 48 hours in advance and may not exceed 5 pages.
validation_note: Confirmed in New Hampshire September 23, 2025 DUR agenda; similar language appears in the April 2026 agenda.

insight_title: Weight-management criteria added Zepbound obstructive sleep apnea and a same-class duplication denial
why_it_matters: This exposes a specific denial lever: using more than one weight-management drug in the class can itself justify denial, even as Zepbound gains an OSA-related indication pathway.
evidence_quote_or_summary: April 2025 minutes say Weight Management criteria updated Zepbound indications to include moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea and obesity, added criteria for denial for using more than one drug within the class, and the motion to accept with amendments passed.
validation_note: Confirmed in New Hampshire April 8, 2025 DUR meeting minutes.

insight_title: Minnesota recommended moving Humira to nonpreferred while preferring multiple adalimumab and ustekinumab biosimilars
drug_or_class: Cytokine and CAM antagonists, Humira, Pyzchiva, Steqeyma, Cyltezo, Yesintek and related biosimilars
why_it_matters: Minnesota's December 2025 draft minutes show a significant biosimilar-favoring shift, including Humira movement to nonpreferred and preferred status for several biosimilar products.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The committee unanimously recommended adding Pyzchiva and Steqeyma forms as preferred, moving adalimumab-adbm/Cyltezo and Yesintek forms to preferred, adding several ustekinumab products as nonpreferred, and moving Humira kit and Humira pen kit to nonpreferred.
validation_note: Confirmed in December 17, 2025 Minnesota DFC draft minutes.

insight_title: DURB recommendations require commissioner acceptance before claims-system implementation
drug_or_class: Medical Exception Program standards / pharmaceutical services claims processing
why_it_matters: New Jersey's public DURB page makes clear that Board recommendations are not self-executing. The operational access change occurs only once standards are accepted and incorporated into claims processing.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The NJDUR page says the DURB recommends standards for the Commissioners of Human Services and Health and Senior Services to consider for approval; once accepted, those standards are incorporated into the State's claims processing system for pharmaceutical services.
validation_note: Confirmed in New Jersey DURB page; HTML source has no page number.
